questions.question_text: The points $A(2,-3)$, $B(7,1)$ and $C(3,6)$ are given. Is $\angle ABC$ a right angle?

options.why: Tested the angle at $A$ instead of at $B$; both vectors must start at the vertex being tested.
Made both products positive, using $20+20$ instead of $20-20$.

options.text: Yes, because $\overrightarrow{BA}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}$ have equal magnitudes
options.why: Equal side lengths make the triangle isosceles; only a zero dot product shows a right angle.

questions.solution_text:
$\overrightarrow{BA}=(2-7,\,-3-1)=\begin{pmatrix}-5\\-4\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{BC}=(3-7,\,6-1)=\begin{pmatrix}-4\\5\end{pmatrix}$
$\overrightarrow{BA}\cdot\overrightarrow{BC}$
$=(-5)(-4)+(-4)(5)$
$=20-20$
$=0$
The dot product is zero, so $\angle ABC=90^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text: For which values of $t$ are $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}t+1\\t+1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}t\\5\end{pmatrix}$ perpendicular?

options.why: Kept $t=-1$, which makes $\underset{\sim}{u}$ the zero vector; the zero vector has no direction, so the test does not apply.
Rejected the wrong root; it is $t=-1$ that makes $\underset{\sim}{u}$ the zero vector.
Sign slip when solving $(t+1)(t+5)=0$; the roots of $(t+1)(t+5)$ are negative.

questions.solution_text:
$(t+1)(t)+(t+1)(5)=0$
$(t+1)(t+5)=0$
$t=-1$ or $t=-5$
When $t=-1$, $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\0\end{pmatrix}$, which has no direction and so cannot be perpendicular to $\underset{\sim}{v}$.
$t=-5$
